text.p: Australian bonds extended Wednesday's underperformance against dollar bond bloc yields with sentiment remaining severely jarred after the RBA's Bulletin dampened hopes of an easing in policy, traders said.
The Australian 10-year yield spread to the U.S. widened to its highest level in a month and its margin over New Zealand grew further, having gone to a premium on Wednesday.
The local market was relatively stable against Canadian debt. The Bank of Canada eased policy by 25 basis points on Wednesday, although the only surprise there being in its timing.
The domestic bond yield curve flattened again as the short-end continued to underperform as the market partly unwound its expectations of a domestic official interest rate cut.

Meanwhile, the U.S. Treasury market faces a barrage of data later today. U.S. bonds ended slightly easier on Wednesday after failing to follow-through a rally on its CPI, which came in line with expectations.
